message:
fix(host): a supervisor standing down now checks that its child went

The handoff exit called DestroyWindow and left the child to WM_DESTROY. Not the
wrong order -- just unverified. On 2026-09-11 a GNLinkStream created one second
after the acknowledgement outlived the host that owned it and kept UDP 43000 and
3478; the host the updater started next could not bind, died with code 3, and
retried to streak=36 until the machine was unusable. Twice. Recovery took the user
killing the orphan by hand.

And nothing said so. The updater reported only that it could not ask some pid to
stop, so the chain from "a child was left behind" to "the next host cannot start"
was broken in the log.

So Stop() reports what it achieved, the handoff path stops the child before
destroying the window and writes down whether it went, and a child that outlived
its parent is called out with its consequence -- the next host may fail to bind.
The early-return path no longer just returns: it looks, and asks again if
something is still there.

Narrow on purpose: no architecture change, no escalation to TerminateProcess, no
killing by name, and the updater does not touch anybody else's children. A
supervisor tidies up its own.

The four new checks are labelled (static) because that is what they are -- they
read the source and confirm the wiring. They do not show that the real Host does
this when it really stands down; only running it can, and that is the field
re-test. The existing real-process counterexample (orphan exits / orphan stays,
plus the negative control) is unchanged.

Also corrects four claims of mine that were graded too high: "no in-app run has
ever completed" is withdrawn as a blanket statement (the user reported a
successful Host update; what we could not observe is separated as unconfirmed);
"absent log means it did not run" and "absent result: means run() did not return"
are possibilities, not findings; and https is not rolled back to wholly unverified
-- healthz succeeds over the product's WinHTTP, so the unverified part is the
client's authenticated path and the field.

The advice to fix the office PC with one Host update is withdrawn: the orphan
defect can bite there too.
